claims.text: stage-4 cluster-migration-plan.md: plan only, not run; moves Đơn Hàng to the managed cluster of ADR 0022; new cluster built beside the old, then traffic switched; the old cluster keeps running as the way back until the move is checked; durations assumed until a staging rehearsal.

Plan: Kubernetes objects are not copied; Argo CD on the new cluster rebuilds them from the config repository, as dr-drill.sh rebuilds staging; no etcd snapshot is carried over because it brings the old cluster's nodes, addresses and Secrets; only data moves.
An etcd snapshot holds the cluster's API objects (including Secrets), not the data stored on volumes.
claims.source_hint: Kubernetes docs: Operating etcd clusters for Kubernetes > Backing up an etcd cluster; k8s.l3.etcd-snapshots summary line 4

claims.text: Plan table: four per-cluster differences, each changed in the config repository by its own pull request before the new cluster syncs: sealing key, StorageClass, Gateway address, cluster code (kind-cluster module -> managed cluster module in deploy/tofu/envs/production/cluster/main.tf).

New cluster gets a new sealing key pair; every SealedSecret of the overlay is sealed again with seal-secrets.sh and the new certificate, which carries the key's public half; only the controller holding the matching private key can decrypt a SealedSecret.
claims.source_hint: cluster-migration-plan.md line 24 @ stage-4; Sealed Secrets README (controller private key decrypts; kubeseal --cert)

claims.text: Volumes of db, rabbitmq and db-backups set no storageClassName today, so they get the cluster's default StorageClass; on the new cluster the overlay names the provider's StorageClass for them.
claims.source_hint: cluster-migration-plan.md line 25 @ stage-4; Kubernetes docs: Persistent Volumes > Class (PVC without storageClassName uses default StorageClass)

claims.text: Traefik is the controller serving the Gateway (kubernetesGateway provider on); today NodePorts 30080 and 30443; new cluster: the provider's load balancer; changes apps/traefik.yaml (Service type) and the DNS records of the two production names (api and login).

Plan data: new PostgreSQL restored from the latest base backup, then reads on in the archived WAL; once caught up writes stop (15 min, assumed) by a commit setting the old cluster's api to 0 replicas, so no new order or message is created.

With automated sync and selfHeal: true (as in apps/staging.yaml), Argo CD syncs again when live objects drift from Git, so a kubectl scale is reverted to the replica count in Git; hence writes stop by a commit.
claims.source_hint: Argo CD docs: Automated Sync Policy > Automatic Self-Healing; deploy/gitops/config-repo/apps/staging.yaml @ stage-4; plan lines 35-36

claims.text: Plan RabbitMQ: during the stop Notifications and Payments on the old cluster keep running until queues are empty, then go to 0 by commit; messages in the dead-letter queue are handled first; no message is left in the old cluster's queues.

Plan: then wait for the last WAL to be applied to the new database and open it for writes; Redis holds only cache, is not moved and refills on the new cluster; so no order confirmed to a customer is lost.

Plan cutover: sync + catch-up + test via the new Gateway address; stop writes, drain queues, last WAL; switch DNS, open writes; old cluster kept without traffic. Before step 3, going back = no DNS switch (and revert the write-stop commits); after, new orders exist only on the new cluster.

Plan scope: only the cluster changes; self-run components (PostgreSQL, RabbitMQ, Keycloak, per self-run-components.md) move as they run; switching them to managed services is later, one component per release, so a failure points to one change.

Plan rehearsal: before production, the whole plan runs on a second staging cluster, moving staging data and timing each step; the measured write stop decides the move window and how far ahead shops are told (5 working days, assumed).
dr-drill.sh rebuilds staging through OpenTofu, the controllers, the Git server from a mirror clone and Argo CD's Application from apps/staging.yaml until Synced/Healthy; no etcd snapshot is used.
dr-drill.sh --without-sealing-key: the controller cannot open the SealedSecrets, no Secret db or api is created, and db's Pod waits with reason CreateContainerConfigError.
Opinion: after DNS has switched and writes opened, fix the problem on the new cluster with a new change unless orders are being lost, because going back then means moving data the other way.

Opinion (trade-offs table, choices): a move that changes cluster and database together leaves a failure ambiguous between the two; restoring a snapshot brings whatever the old cluster held, so a failure may come from it; keep the database switch for a later release.
Production today runs on the cluster built by the kind-cluster module (deploy/tofu/envs/production/cluster/main.tf), which the move replaces with a managed cluster module.

Recovery started with recovery.signal (as db/pitr/start.sh, used by pitr.sh) ends at the end of the archived WAL; a server in standby mode keeps fetching new archived segments with restore_command and does not stop.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: Server Configuration > Write Ahead Log > Archive Recovery (19.5.5); db/pitr/start.sh lines 10-22 @ stage-4

claims.text: pg_switch_wal() closes the current WAL segment so it is archived now, not after archive_timeout; pitr.sh calls it before recovering.
claims.source_hint: PostgreSQL docs: Functions > Backup Control Functions (pg_switch_wal); scripts/devops/pitr.sh lines 35-41 @ stage-4

claims.text: At stage-4 only the Compose db archives WAL (archive_mode, archive_command, archive_timeout); the in-cluster production db keeps its data in an emptyDir and archives no WAL.
The plan does not say how the write-stop commit reaches only the old cluster, nor what starts the new api when writes open.
